## Daily Checks

**When:** Every morning, first thing  
**Time Required:** 5 minutes  
**Owner:** Whoever is on-call that day

### Procedure

```bash
# SSH into app-1
ssh root@app-1-ip

# Check both VMs are responding
ping -c 1 app-1-ip
ping -c 1 db-1-ip

# Check disk space (should be >20% free)
df -h

# Check if Laravel app is responding
curl -I https://marketplace.example.com

# Check queue worker is running
supervisorctl status laravel-worker

# Check MySQL is running
systemctl status mysql

# Check Uptime Kuma is running
systemctl status uptime-kuma
```

**Success looks like:**
- Both pings succeed
- `df -h` shows >20% free on all partitions
- `curl` returns HTTP 200
- `supervisorctl status` shows `laravel-worker RUNNING`
- `systemctl status mysql` shows `active (running)`
- `systemctl status uptime-kuma` shows `active (running)`

**If anything fails:** Go to [Emergency Procedures](#emergency-procedures)

## Certificate Renewal

**When:** Automatically, but verify monthly  
**Time Required:** 2 minutes  
**Owner:** Either developer

### Why This Matters

Your TLS certificate expires every 90 days. Let's Encrypt automatically renews it, but if renewal fails silently, your site will become inaccessible.

### Procedure

```bash
ssh root@app-1-ip

# Check when certificate expires
certbot certificates

# Look for "Expiry Date" in the output
```

**Success looks like:**
- Expiry date is >30 days away
- If expiry is <30 days away, manually renew:

```bash
certbot renew --force-renewal
systemctl reload nginx
```

**If renewal fails:**
- Check logs: `cat /var/log/letsencrypt/letsencrypt.log`
- Escalate to DevOps consultant

## Database Backup Verification

**When:** Every Monday morning  
**Time Required:** 10 minutes  
**Owner:** Either developer

### Why This Matters

Backups run automatically every night, but you need to verify they're actually working. A silent backup failure is a disaster.

### Procedure

```bash
ssh root@db-1-ip

# Check the last backup file exists and is recent
ls -lh /var/backups/mysql/ | head -5

# The most recent file should be from yesterday
# Example output:
# -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 245M Jan 15 02:30 marketplace-2024-01-15.sql.gz
```

**Success looks like:**
- Most recent file is from yesterday
- File size is >100MB (your database is not empty)
- File is readable: `gunzip -t /var/backups/mysql/marketplace-2024-01-15.sql.gz`

**If the test fails:**
```bash
# Check if rclone upload is working
rclone ls b2:marketplace-backups | head -5

# Should show recent files like:
# marketplace-2024-01-15.sql.gz
```

**If backups are missing:**
- Check cron job: `crontab -l`
- Check logs: `tail -50 /var/log/syslog | grep rclone`
- Escalate to DevOps consultant

## Deployment

**When:** During business hours only (9 AM–6 PM Bangladesh time)  
**Time Required:** 10 minutes  
**Owner:** Either developer

### Pre-Deployment Checklist

- [ ] Code is merged to `main` branch
- [ ] All tests pass locally
- [ ] You have a rollback plan (previous commit hash)
- [ ] You've notified the team in Slack

### Procedure

```bash
ssh root@app-1-ip

# Go to app directory
cd /var/www/marketplace

# Pull latest code
git pull origin main

# Install/update dependencies
composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader

# Run migrations
php artisan migrate --force

# Clear caches
php artisan config:cache
php artisan route:cache
php artisan view:cache

# Restart queue worker
supervisorctl restart laravel-worker

# Reload PHP-FPM
systemctl reload php8.2-fpm

# Test the site
curl -I https://marketplace.example.com
```

**Success looks like:**
- `git pull` completes without conflicts
- `composer install` completes without errors
- `php artisan migrate` shows "Migrated" or "Nothing to migrate"
- `curl` returns HTTP 200

**If something fails:**

```bash
# Rollback to previous version
git checkout [previous-commit-hash]
composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader
php artisan migrate --force
supervisorctl restart laravel-worker
systemctl reload php8.2-fpm

# Notify team and escalate
```

---

## Emergency Procedures

### The Site Is Down (HTTP 500 or no response)

**Time to fix:** 15 minutes  
**Owner:** Whoever is available

```bash
ssh root@app-1-ip

# Step 1: Check if app-1 is responding at all
ping -c 1 app-1-ip

# If no response, restart the VM from Hetzner Cloud console
# Wait 2 minutes, then continue

# Step 2: Check PHP-FPM
systemctl status php8.2-fpm

# If not running:
systemctl start php8.2-fpm

# Step 3: Check nginx
systemctl status nginx

# If not running:
systemctl start nginx

# Step 4: Check Laravel logs
tail -100 /var/www/marketplace/storage/logs/laravel.log

# Step 5: Check disk space
df -h

# If any partition is >90% full, escalate immediately
```

**If you see errors in the logs:**
- Copy the error message
- Check if it's a recent code change (ask the other developer)
- If yes, rollback using [Deployment](#deployment) procedure
- If no, escalate to DevOps consultant

**If disk is full:**
- Do NOT delete files yourself
- Escalate immediately

### Queue Worker Is Not Processing Jobs

**Time to fix:** 5 minutes

```bash
ssh root@app-1-ip

# Check status
supervisorctl status laravel-worker

# If it says STOPPED:
supervisorctl start laravel-worker

# If it says FATAL or BACKOFF:
supervisorctl restart laravel-worker

# Check logs
tail -50 /var/log/supervisor/laravel-worker-stderr.log

# If there are errors, check Laravel logs
tail -100 /var/www/marketplace/storage/logs/laravel.log
```

**If errors persist:**
- Escalate to DevOps consultant

### Database Is Slow or Unresponsive

**Time to fix:** 10 minutes

```bash
ssh root@db-1-ip

# Check if MySQL is running
systemctl status mysql

# If not running:
systemctl start mysql

# Check disk space
df -h

# If >90% full, escalate immediately

# Check MySQL logs
tail -50 /var/log/mysql/error.log

# Check active connections
mysql -u root -p[password] -e "SHOW PROCESSLIST;"

# If there are many sleeping connections, they'll clear automatically
# If there are long-running queries, ask the developers if they're expected
```

**If MySQL won't start:**
- Check logs: `tail -100 /var/log/mysql/error.log`
- Escalate to DevOps consultant

### Certificate Is About to Expire (or Already Expired)

**Time to fix:** 5 minutes

```bash
ssh root@app-1-ip

# Force renewal
certbot renew --force-renewal

# Reload nginx
systemctl reload nginx

# Verify
certbot certificates
```

**If renewal fails:**
- Check logs: `tail -50 /var/log/letsencrypt/letsencrypt.log`
- Escalate to DevOps consultant

## Monitoring & Alerts

### Uptime Kuma

Uptime Kuma runs on app-1 and monitors:
- HTTPS endpoint (marketplace.example.com)
- MySQL connectivity
- Disk space on both VMs

**Access:** `https://app-1-ip:3001` (username/password in shared vault)

**When alerts fire:**
- You'll get a Telegram message in the team group
- Check the Uptime Kuma dashboard to see which service failed
- Follow the relevant emergency procedure above

**If Uptime Kuma itself is down:**

```bash
ssh root@app-1-ip

systemctl status uptime-kuma

# If not running:
systemctl start uptime-kuma

# Check logs
journalctl -u uptime-kuma -n 50
```

## Troubleshooting

### "Permission denied" when SSHing

- Check you're using the correct IP address
- Check your SSH key is in `~/.ssh/id_rsa` (or configured in `~/.ssh/config`)
- Ask the other developer for their SSH key setup

### "Connection refused" when accessing the site

```bash
# Check nginx is listening
netstat -tlnp | grep nginx

# Should show:
# tcp  0  0 0.0.0.0:80   0.0.0.0:*  LISTEN
# tcp  0  0 0.0.0.0:443  0.0.0.0:*  LISTEN

# If not, restart nginx
systemctl restart nginx
```

### "SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 2006 MySQL has gone away"

This means the database connection died. Usually temporary.

```bash
# Check MySQL is running
systemctl status mysql

# Restart if needed
systemctl restart mysql

# Restart the queue worker
supervisorctl restart laravel-worker

# Restart PHP-FPM
systemctl reload php8.2-fpm
```

### "Composer install" is very slow

This is normal on first run. It can take 5–10 minutes. Don't interrupt it.

### "git pull" fails with merge conflicts

```bash
# This means someone edited the same file as you
# Ask the other developer what they changed
# Then either:

# Option 1: Keep your changes
git checkout --ours [filename]
git add [filename]
git commit -m "Resolved conflict"

# Option 2: Keep their changes
git checkout --theirs [filename]
git add [filename]
git commit -m "Resolved conflict"

# Then continue with deployment
```

## Quick Reference

### SSH Shortcuts

Add to `~/.ssh/config`:

```
Host app-1
    HostName [app-1-ip]
    User root
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_rsa

Host db-1
    HostName [db-1-ip]
    User root
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_rsa
```

Then: `ssh app-1` instead of `ssh root@[ip]`

### Common Commands

```bash
# Restart everything
ssh app-1 'systemctl restart php8.2-fpm nginx && supervisorctl restart laravel-worker'

# Check all services
ssh app-1 'systemctl status php8.2-fpm nginx uptime-kuma'
ssh db-1 'systemctl status mysql'

# View recent errors
ssh app-1 'tail -100 /var/www/marketplace/storage/logs/laravel.log'

# Check resource usage
ssh app-1 'free -h && df -h'
ssh db-1 'free -h && df -h'
```

---

## Handover Checklist

Before the DevOps engineer leaves, verify:

- [ ] Both developers can SSH into both VMs
- [ ] Both developers can access Uptime Kuma dashboard
- [ ] Both developers have run a test deployment
- [ ] Both developers have verified a backup
- [ ] Both developers have the DevOps consultant's contact info
- [ ] This runbook is printed and posted in the office
- [ ] This runbook is in your shared Slack channel
- [ ] Passwords are in your shared vault (1Password, Bitwarden, etc.)
- [ ] SSH keys are backed up securely
